title: Assessment of Heavy Metal and Microbial Contamination in Soil and Groundwater around a Municipal Solid Waste Dumpsite in Zomba, Malawi
content: The present study assessed heavy metal and microbial contamination in soil and groundwater surrounding a municipal solid waste dumpsite in Zomba, Malawi, and in-vestigated the potential ecological and health risks to nearby communities. During the wet season, groundwater samples showed elevated counts of total coliform (20900 cfu/100 mL), Escherichia coli (3300 cfu/100 mL), Staphylococcus aureus (2500 cfu/100 mL), and Vibrio cholerae (5900 cfu/100 mL), all exceeding Malawi Standards limits. Water samples also contained concerning concentrations of chromium (0.011–0.14 mg/L) and Cadmium (0. 07 – 041 mg/L). In soil, lead ranged from 0.16 to 224.05 mg/kg, copper from 3.03 to 94.86 mg/kg, cadmium from below detectable limit to 0.89 mg/kg, arsenic from below detectable limit to 1.88 mg/kg, and chromium from 0.07 to 0.91 mg/kg. Cancer risk assessment showed exceeded the acceptable CR threshold of 1 × 10-3 for adults, while 40% exceeded this threshold for infants and children, indicating a notable cancer risk, particularly from cadmium exposure.
